business_summary.text: Ambuja Cements, part of the Adani Group, is a leading Indian cement manufacturer with a consolidated capacity of 113.5 MTPA and a target to reach 155 MTPA through organic and inorganic growth.

call_points.text: Volumes are expected to grow ahead of the industry in H2FY27.
Firmed-up expansion of 29.7 MTPA to take capacity to 149 MTPA.
Geopolitical issues added ₹228 per tonne to costs in Q2FY27.
Company remains debt-free with AAA credit ratings.
Green power share reached 61% in Q2FY27.
Higher maintenance costs in Q2 due to planned kiln shutdowns.
Cost optimization initiatives expected to reduce total cement cost by Rs. 150–200 PMT in FY27 from ~Rs. 4,400 PMT in FY26.
Targeting asset utilization increase from 77% to 85% across operational base.
Amalgamation of ACC and Orient with Ambuja awaiting SEBI NOC; expected to complete over FY27.
Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement mergers completed and made effective in March and April 2026.
Net worth stands at ₹71,846 Cr and company remains debt-free with cash and cash equivalents of ₹1,770 Cr.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company (ACL) was entitled to excise duty incentives. ACL has been contending that the said incentives are in the nature of capital receipts and hence not liable to income tax. However, the Income tax department had consistently denied the position and considered these incentives as a taxable receipt. Appeals were filed by ACL against the orders of the Assessing Officer which were pending before the ITAT. In November 2022, the Company received favourable orders from ITAT. However, pending final closure of the matter, the amount of Rs. 372.01 crore (December 31, 2021 – Rs. 372.01 crore) along with interest payable of Rs. 111.18 crore (December 31, 2021 – Rs. 111.18 crore) has been disclosed as contingent liabilities.
tax_litigation.status: No change in the status from last Quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A matter relating to 75% exemption from sales tax, granted by Government of Rajasthan. However, the eligibility of exemption in excess of 25% was contested by the State Government in a similar matter of another Company. In year 2014, pursuant to the unfavourable decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in that similar matter, the sales tax department initiated proceedings for recovery of differential sales tax and interest thereon on the ground that the Company had given an undertaking to deposit the differential amount of sales tax, in case decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court goes against in this matter. Against the total demand of Rs. 247.97 crore, including interest of Rs. 134.45 crore (December 31, 2021 – Rs. 247.97 crore, including interest of Rs. 134.45 crore) the Company deposited Rs. 143.52 crore, including interest of Rs. 30.00 crore (December 31, 2021 – Rs. 143.52 crore, including interest of Rs. 30.00 crore) towards sales tax under protest and filed a Special Leave Petition in the Hon’ble Supreme Court with one of the grounds that the tax exemption was availed by virtue of the order passed by the Board for Industrial & Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) during the relevant period. On Company’s petition, the Hon’ble Supreme Court has granted an interim stay on the balance interest. Based on the advice of external legal counsel, the Company believes that, it has good grounds for a successful appeal. Accordingly, the amount has been disclosed as contingent liability.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Sales Tax Department, State of Rajasthan
tax_litigation.status: No change in the status from last Quarter.

Accordingly. the management has assessed the risk to be remote and reduced the contingent liability for this matter to nil

operating_notes.text: Total cement capacity reached 109 MTPA in FY26.
Cement capacity reached 109 MTPA as of 31st March 2026; targeting ~119 MTPA in H1FY27.
Target to reduce total cement cost by Rs. 150–200 PMT in FY27 from ~Rs. 4,400 PMT in FY26.
Overall consolidated capacity utilisation improved to 77% in Q4FY26; targeting 85% utilisation across base.
Reported a violation of SEBI PIT Regulations by Mr. Kiran Kotian (Finance – Digital) involving 250 shares; penalty of ₹25,005 and disgorgement of ₹1,595 paid to IPEF.
BRSR report for FY2025-26 assured by SGS India with reasonable assurance on BRSR Core.
Cement capacity stood at 109 MTPA as of June 30, 2026, and is expected to reach 119 MTPA by FY27.
Commissioned 1.2 MTPA brownfield cement grinding unit at Dahej, taking total consolidated capacity to 110.05 MTPA.
Commissioned 2.4 MTPA greenfield grinding unit at Salai Banwa (UP) and 3.0 MTPA blending unit (1 MTPA additional capacity) at Kalamboli (Maharashtra), taking consolidated capacity to 113.45 MTPA.
Authorised share capital increased to ₹10,904 Cr following amalgamations.
US DOJ dropped all charges against a non-executive director on August 10, 2026.
Commissioned 4.6 MTPA capacity in Q2 at Dahej (1.2 MTPA), Salai Banwa (2.4 MTPA), and Kalamboli (1.0 MTPA).
Green power share increased to 61% in Q2FY27.
Impact of escalated geopolitical issues estimated at ~₹228 per tonne in Q2FY27.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹10,915.47 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹1,830.15 Cr.
Ambuja Cements reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹40,656 Cr and net profit of ₹4,728.18 Cr with annual volumes reaching 73.7 MnT.
Ambuja Cements presented FY26 presentation outlining 109 MTPA capacity, H1FY27 expansion target of ~119 MTPA, and ₹150–200 PMT cost reduction goal for FY27.
Manish Mistry, Chairman, uploaded audio recording of Analysts/Investors Call on Audited Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated) for Q4FY26 and FY26 on May 4, 2026.
Ambuja Cements reported a SEBI PIT Regulation violation by a designated person involving 250 shares and a ₹25,005 penalty.
Ambuja Cements announced scheduled institutional investor interactions for June 2026.
Adani Enterprises Limited, as promoter, declared no new encumbrances on Ambuja Cements Limited shares as of March 31, 2026, under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
On May 30, 2026, Ambuja Cements submitted its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY2025-26.
Ambuja Cements received 'No Objection' from NSE and BSE for its proposed merger with ACC Limited on June 4, 2026.
Ambuja Cements received exchange observation letters for the proposed amalgamation of Orient Cement on June 4, 2026.
Ambuja Cements received an NCLT Ahmedabad bench order on July 20, 2026, to convene a shareholder meeting on September 28, 2026, for the amalgamation of Orient Cement.
Q1FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹9,500 Cr (-7.7% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹577 Cr.
Ambuja Cements reported Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹9,500 Cr and net profit of ₹660 Cr.
ICRA assigned [ICRA]AAA (Stable) and [ICRA]A1+ ratings to Ambuja Cements' ₹7,000 crore bank facilities.
Ambuja Cements commissioned a 1.2 MTPA brownfield cement grinding unit at Dahej through its subsidiary, taking total capacity to 110.05 MTPA.
Ambuja Cements received IND AAA/Stable and IND A1+ ratings from India Ratings for ₹7,000 crore bank facilities on August 20, 2026.
Ambuja Cements announced a court-convened meeting of equity shareholders for September 28, 2026, to approve the scheme of amalgamation of Orient Cement Limited.
Ambuja Cements announced that its equity shareholders approved the scheme of amalgamation with Orient Cement Limited at the NCLT-convened meeting held on September 28, 2026.
Ambuja Cements announced the commissioning of 5.4 MTPA of new grinding and blending capacity by subsidiaries, taking consolidated capacity to 113.45 MTPA.
Ambuja Cements approved the acquisition of a 26% stake in SWE Renewables for ₹33.75 Cr and reported a standalone Q2 profit of ₹114 Cr.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹9,197 Cr (+0.2% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹193 Cr (includes ₹5 Cr from discontinued operations; continuing operations ₹231 Cr).
Ambuja Cements reported Q2FY27 consolidated EBITDA of ₹1,271 Cr and reached 113.5 MTPA capacity following the commissioning of 4.6 MTPA of new units.
